page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, it features 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware-level features such as AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. This instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25% at 2669.58. However, multi-core and memory performance are significantly constrained. The stress-ng multi-core metric falls into the bottom 25% at 2672.78, and the Geekbench multi-core score is in the bottom 10% at 1812.0. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 126.7 GB/sec (bottom 10%) and large block uncached write bandwidth at 20.4 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels, while database operations and static web serving throughput are weak, placing in the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated x86_64 compute resources, though its low memory bandwidth and weak multi-core scaling present clear tradeoffs. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and simple background utility tasks that do not demand high memory throughput or parallel processing power.
